    """
    Tests that problematic private escape sequences (\x1b0 - \x1b?) are ignored
    by the ANSI parser, preventing them from being rendered as styled tokens.
    """
    decoder = AnsiDecoder()
    
    # Test sequence \x1b0
    problem_sequence_0 = "\x1b0"
    
    # Test sequence \x1b?
    problem_sequence_q = "\x1b?"
    
    # Test sequence \x1b[1m (Normal SGR)
    normal_sequence_1 = "\x1b[1m"
    
    # Test sequence \x1b[?25l (cursor visibility toggle, should be ignored)
    cursor_toggle = "\x1b[?25l"

    # Test 1: \x1b0
    # If the fix works, \x1b0 should be treated as plain text.
    text_0 = decoder.decode_line(problem_sequence_0)
    assert isinstance(text_0, Text)
    assert text_0.plain == problem_sequence_0
    assert text_0.style is None

    # Test 2: \x1b?
    text_q = decoder.decode_line(problem_sequence_q)
    assert isinstance(text_q, Text)
    assert text_q.plain == problem_sequence_q
    assert text_q.style is None

    # Test 3: \x1b[1m (Normal SGR)
    text_1 = decoder.decode_line(normal_sequence_1)
    assert isinstance(text_1, Text)
    # The Text object should contain one run of styled text
    assert len(text_1.runs) == 1
    assert text_1.runs[0].style.name == "bold"

    # Test 4: \x1b[?25l (Cursor toggle - should be ignored)
    text_cursor = decoder.decode_line(cursor_toggle)
    assert isinstance(text_cursor, Text)
    assert text_cursor.plain == cursor_toggle
    assert text_cursor.style is None

    # Test 5: Mixed sequence
    mixed_sequence = f"Start\n{problem_sequence_0}Middle\n{normal_sequence_1}End\n{problem_sequence_q}Final"
    text_mixed = decoder.decode_line(mixed_sequence)
    
    # Check the resulting Text object structure
    # It should contain multiple runs/plain parts.
    
    # Since the tokenizer now treats \x1b0 and \x1b? as plain text, 
    # the resulting Text object should reflect this.
    
    # We expect 7 runs/plain parts:
    # 1. "Start\n" (plain)
    # 2. "\x1b0" (plain)
    # 3. "Middle\n" (plain)
    # 4. "\x1b[1m" (styled run)
    # 5. "End\n" (plain)
    # 6. "\x1b?" (plain)
    # 7. "Final" (plain)
    
    # This is hard to assert precisely without knowing how Text.runs handles concatenation 
    # of plain text and styled runs when the plain text itself contains control characters.
    
    # A simpler check: ensure the output contains the literal sequences and the style is correct for the SGR part.
    
    # Check for the presence of the literal sequences in the rendered text (if we could render it).
    # Since we are testing the object structure, we check the runs.
    
    # The Text object should have at least 7 segments (plain or styled).
    assert len(text_mixed.runs) >= 7
    
    # Check that the SGR part is correctly identified as a run
    sgr_run_found = any(run.style.name == "bold" for run in text_mixed.runs)
    assert sgr_run_found
    
    # Check that the problematic sequences are present as plain text segments
    plain_segments = [segment for segment in text_mixed.runs if segment.plain]
    assert problem_sequence_0 in plain_segments
    assert problem_sequence_q in plain_segments
